models.name: Kokoro 82M · PyTorch
models.description: Small, natural-sounding text-to-speech model with 54 voices across eight languages. This is the original PyTorch release with one voice (af_heart). The Kokoro engine runs it through a Python with the kokoro package, without network access. English voices only in this version.

notes: The publisher does not state hardware requirements for this format.

models.name: Qwen3-TTS 1.7B Base · bf16
models.description: Qwen3-TTS Base, 1.7 billion parameters, bf16 weights converted for MLX. Clones a voice from a short reference recording and its exact transcript, so every narration sounds like the same speaker. The Qwen3-TTS engine uses it with a voice profile, through a Python with mlx-audio, without network access. Ten languages.

notes: Runs through MLX, so on Macs with Apple Silicon only. The publisher states no memory requirement.
Used during development on an Apple M4 Pro with 24 GB of unified memory.

inferenceTests.hardware: Apple M4 Pro, 24 GB unified memory

models.name: LTX-2.3 22B Distilled 1.1
models.description: Lightricks' 22-billion-parameter video model, distilled for fewer sampling steps; generates video from text or from a still image. This is the original full-precision release. The Draw Things app uses its own converted copy, which this does not replace, and no engine in Framebop Studio loads this file directly.

notes: No hardware requirement for this file is published on its model page, so compatibility cannot be judged.

models.name: Stable Diffusion 1.5 · Q8_0 GGUF
models.description: The original Stable Diffusion 1.5 (pruned, EMA weights), converted to GGUF and quantized to 8 bits by second-state for stable-diffusion.cpp. Small and well understood: the model Framebop's own image engine is first checked with. 512 × 512 pictures.

notes: The publisher states no hardware requirements.

presets.note: Used for the first picture made by Framebop's own image engine.

inferenceTests.hardware: Apple M4 Pro, 24 GB unified memory
inferenceTests.detail: One 512 × 512 picture, 20 steps, Euler ancestral, guidance 7, through stable-diffusion.cpp master-929-3f8527a: 86 seconds including about 20 seconds of loading; the runtime reported its Metal backend.

inferenceTests.hardware: Apple M4 Pro, 24 GB unified memory
inferenceTests.detail: The same picture with flash attention in the diffusion model (--diffusion-fa): 24 seconds in total (20.5 s sampling, 3.3 s decoding), 2.4 GB peak memory; SSIM 0.999 against the run without it.

models.name: Wan 2.2 TI2V 5B (Q4_K_M)
models.description: Alibaba's Wan 2.2 video model with 5 billion parameters, which makes clips from a still picture or from text alone. This is QuantStack's GGUF conversion, quantized to 4 bits, with the model's own VAE. Framebop's clip engine runs it with stable-diffusion.cpp; the umt5-xxl text encoder it reads prompts with is installed with it. Clips of up to five seconds at 24 frames a second, 832 × 480.

notes: The publisher of this conversion states no hardware requirements.

license.name: Apache License 2.0
license.summary: Permissive: use, modification and redistribution, including commercial, with notice.

presets.label: 832 × 480, 20 steps
presets.description: The settings Wan 2.2 TI2V 5B's authors use, at 480p: guidance 5, flow shift 5, 24 frames a second.
presets.note: Sampling worked on an M4 Pro (about 40 s a step); decoding the frames did not finish in 55 minutes.

models.name: umt5-xxl text encoder (Q4_K_M)
models.description: Google's multilingual umt5-xxl encoder, which turns a prompt into what Wan video models read. city96's GGUF conversion, quantized to 4 bits. It makes nothing on its own: Framebop's clip engine needs it next to Wan 2.2 TI2V 5B.

notes: The publisher states no hardware requirements.

models.name: LTX-2.3 Distilled · MLX Q4
models.description: Local Apple Silicon video using the MLX split pack. Requires a separately configured Python runtime and the shared Gemma text encoder. Low-memory streaming, silent clips, 24 fps, up to five seconds. The conservative file list is the one used for the independent benchmark.

notes: The independent M4 Pro 24 GiB run used low-memory streaming. System swap was already in use; a successful run is not a guarantee for every machine or workload.
